The first current-source control run used Actions source `b614864ba9da55c13662894b6ef3c8515d9fdb25` / tree `6fa4f5c1e9837a0d893868255575b355b3977fae`, RCC3 binary `7e588c01751ca2ae15ba13ef67f2f4b7567697a5a8389737059a73936f509428`, and the exact frozen two-case fixture inventory in config SHA256 `8c5da5be25ebfcf86f286ee9f93ddad328c68b3243b0935ec5937c93376bb948`. The real publication/details identity-pair case passed once; the staged Action case started but has no terminal result.

The sampled isolated namespace crossed the 2.35 GiB operational stop threshold (2,529,735,510 measured bytes). The bounded stop targeted only the recorded pytest PID/create-time. The original helper then raised ProcessTreeCleanupError; final descendant and reader evidence is absent. Primary capacity failure and cleanup failure remain separate. The raw publication receipt is retained (`22121727f88ac95fbbef644231efb93884cff54f8ca7281e79b089c67eafa6bd`). Independent failure review SHA256 `d14c888b448f5ad59dcfc5ae26b75bda80901b297f8735902146fc6536227fc3` requires STOP: released18.19.5 and candidate7276/18.19.6 have NOT_RUN.

Read-only diagnosis found two independent client homes retaining roughly 1.2 GB each of package-cache data, including duplicate conda repodata, while provider artifacts were much smaller. We are implementing explicit isolated sharing of only the once-owned package cache, preserving per-case holotree, artifact/provider and origin assertions, cold first acquisition, and the existing capacity ceiling. This is a prospective fixture fix, not evidence of RCC-version incompatibility or a gate waiver. Original failed state, source, logs and receipts are preserved. Failure-path supervisor/cleanup metadata retention is also being corrected without changing the frozen helper.

The tested source-admission contract and exact acquired RCC5/7276 identities below remain unchanged. Broad persistent reuse, reload/drain, provider recovery, private fixture and production-release gates remain open.

---

Actions compatibility execution is active under existing Actions #133/#134/#139/#143 and PR #221/#308 ownership. The approved change removes the v18.19.3-only test admission restriction while retaining all production/download/build defaults at v18.19.3.

Current source candidate: `b614864ba9da55c13662894b6ef3c8515d9fdb25`, tree `6fa4f5c1e9837a0d893868255575b355b3977fae`. Focused source checks: 180 passed, one existing opt-in skip, three deselected; lint/types passed. Independent review and configured full source gate are in progress. This is source validation, not new-binary functionality qualification.

The tested admission contract requires an explicit isolated test selector, an operator-approved immutable provenance tuple, exact native SHA256 checked before probe/cache/acquire/execute, observed version/platform and required feature surface. Unknown selectors, missing explicit binaries, wrong native bytes/platform and stale or co-mutated descriptors fail closed before fallback downloads or artifact access. Existing v18.19.3 behavior is preserved. A binary's version output alone cannot qualify it.

Acquired test-only Linux amd64 binaries:

- Released v18.19.5, asset 549249380, 22,360,226 bytes, SHA256 `1a617ad7c736fa67c605e20e5ebe3c7d54b02cd548f733e05c809cf49a48db1e`; embedded/tag source `d1aec7d0bb897a81274423c7a6bb747233f9c263`, Go 1.26.5, `vcs.modified=true`. The cause of modification and equivalence to unchanged source are UNKNOWN and remain blockers to clean-source/production promotion.
- v18.19.6 exact source candidate `727c1ff8b679cdbbe12836e53c87734a1edb0071`, tree `cfae5c5ee9df0e5031e8e9ae37040b5c98ac6152`; successful push run 38105340592, native artifact 11689755940 and Linux receipt artifact 11689851536. Selected binary 22,384,802 bytes, SHA256 `be55dadc391ae4ac7dd38356755a1698c595fdf41bd4a0141f8df7cc9d29f00e`, Go 1.26.9, `vcs.modified=false`. No v18.19.6 release/tag is assumed.

The originals and all ZIP members/checksum rows were verified without executing newer RCC. The first conditional execution wave uses the existing real published-artifact identity and managed staged-Action fixtures, first v18.19.3 control, then released 5, then source727 candidate6, once each with isolated homes/provider/temporary state and bounded execution/owned cleanup. Exact source/binary/fixture/receipt hashes will accompany any accepted result.

Persistent reuse, source reload, generation drain and provider recovery require their own measured fixture receipts; this two-case wave cannot establish them by inference. Action natural exit, intentional persistent-worker disposal, lease terminal status and actual typed cleanup are recorded separately. No performance comparison, materializer selection, release acceptance or issue closure is claimed. This comment will be updated with the first actual result or failure.
